topic: Why a QR code still works with a logo on top

claims.claim: QR codes use Reed-Solomon error correction; level H restores roughly 30% of codewords (L 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30%).
30% is a share of codewords, not of visible area; measured safe centred logo at level H is ~15-17% of the area.
sources: https://qrdx.dev/blog/qr-code-scan-study (H: 15.5% of area read in 80%+ of captures)

claims.claim: Glare, dirt, scratches consume the same correction budget.
Finder patterns are not covered by error correction; covering one breaks detection.
sources: https://mostlyqr.com/blog/qr-code-logo-size (top-left finder patch fails at 1% at level H)

claims.claim: Reed-Solomon codes (1960) also protect audio CDs (CIRC).

verification_extra: The QR drawn in the video is a real level-H code for https://youtube.com/@thatsthemechanism generated with node-qrcode (MIT).
